static_traits.name: Li Ze
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to talk with, but has not shared the self-doubt with them; since the competition, began avoiding socializing and interaction with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, low mood; able to cooperate in exploring negative thoughts, but self-negation and pessimistic attitude are evident

basic_info.main_problem: After recently failing to win a swimming competition, I feel discouraged and inadequate; this 'not good enough' feeling has continued since the competition and affects many areas of my life.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent inferiority and self-doubt have affected daily life and overall health; seeks counseling to cope with these problems.
growth_experiences: At an important swimming competition, the client failed to win the trophy (originally expected to win; pre-competition stress was relatively high); since the competition, the client has repeatedly recalled mistakes, forming persistent inferiority and self-doubt, affecting sleep, self-care, social life, and work confidence.

core_beliefs: Worth exists only in being first

special_situations.event: Not winning a trophy at a swimming competition (failing to win the championship as wished)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not get first place, it means I have failed, I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ties worth to winning and losing, repeatedly replays mistakes after matches, and reduces chances of being evaluated by avoiding socializing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never be the best

special_situations.event: Recalling and reviewing game performance after the match
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is a mistake or imperfection in my performance, it proves the whole thing is not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing on mistakes and shortcomings, ignoring objective performance and existing achievements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, it is not enough

special_situations.event: Moments in training when performance is occasionally decent and feels 'okay'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not consistently taking first place, these brief good states do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Disqualifying positive experiences and turning attention back to shortcomings and failures
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is nothing; I am still far from first place

special_situations.event: Thinking about work tasks or challenges in other areas of life
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Not getting first place in one field means I will also be no good in other areas
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Viewing oneself with a global negative evaluation, reducing attempts and investment

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain recognition and a sense of worth through excellent performance and victory
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being belittled, being seen as not good enough, thus losing self-worth
defense_goal: Maintains self-worth boundaries with 'must be first', avoiding feelings of shame and being negated
Reducing outside evaluation by avoiding social contact, to maintain psychological safety

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who is not good enough and needs victories to prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: Picky reviewers/others who judge people by success or failure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites focusing on the positive side or practicing cognitive restructuring
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes these methods are 'useless for me / I cannot change anyway', in order to maintain the existing belief that 'I am not good enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in a helpless and negative tone, such as 'I tried, it did not work', emphasizing difficulties and limitations and reducing emotional investment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about topics of sharing feelings with friends or seeking support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizes the potential discomfort of being judged / compared, avoiding outward expression and help-seeking
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses with self-blaming and negating statements (such as 'it is all because I am incapable'), with a low tone, reducing openness and detail disclosure.

manifestations: Swimming, once loved, became a burden after failure, making it hard to experience value and meaning from it
Self-worth overly tied to first place, process and growth are ignored
outcomes: Increased frustration and sense of hopelessness
Decreased drive, wanting to give up trying

manifestations: Avoids socializing and interacting with friends
Having close friends to talk to but not having shared one's self-doubt
outcomes: Decreased support, worsening sense of isolation

manifestations: Bound by introjected rules such as 'must win first place'
Difficulty allowing room for imperfection and gradual improvement
outcomes: Behaviorally reducing attempts and engagement, tending to give up

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats 'only first place counts as good' as a rigid standard
Defining self-worth entirely by winning and losing

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly self-blaming 'I am not good enough' 'I will never be the best'
Pessimistic and hesitant about trying to change

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not sharing self-doubt with close friends, turning energy into self-reproach
Avoiding socializing to reduce the chance of being judged

exception_events.target_problem: After competitions, when thinking about swimming performance or training, the client is usually trapped by inferiority and self-doubt, finds it hard to see anything positive, and has reduced motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a few post-game training sessions, the client felt they were 'okay', did not wholly negate their current performance as before, and briefly experienced a more acceptable state.
exception_events.reason: Different context: training has less pressure than competitions; different approach: at the time, the client focused more on present movements and process rather than results; therefore it was easier to notice small progress.

positive_force: A stable love of swimming and willingness to commit to it
Having past successful experiences as a resource
Has a few friends who can be relied on (though this route has not yet been used)
Willing to try identifying and challenging negative thoughts, accepting the possibility of cognitive restructuring
Able to notice a few positive moments (the 'okay' experience in training)
negative_force: Marked cognitive distortions such as all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering, and fortune-telling
Self-worth overly dependent on winning and losing and first place
Avoiding social contact leaves the support system unused and increases isolation
Rumination on failure and self-blame worsen negative emotions, sleep and self-care decline
Insufficient hope for change, tending to give up in advance

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly ruminates over game mistakes and engages in self-negation (such as 'I am not good enough' and 'I will never be the best')
antecedent: Thinking about swimming competition results or related cues
target_behavior.core_reason: Binds personal value to winning and losing, showing cognitive biases of mental filtering and catastrophizing / fortune telling to explain failure
target_behavior.function: In the short term, obtains an illusion of 'understanding the cause / a sense of control' through self-blame and rumination, avoiding facing uncertainty and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and despair worsen, sleep disturbed, motivation declines, affecting confidence at work and in other life domains

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids socializing and interacting with friends
antecedent: Receiving a social invitation or thinking about meeting friends
Thinking of possible evaluations by others
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being seen as not good enough and failing in comparisons, shame and inferiority drive avoidance
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation and uncomfortable emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, increased loneliness, negative emotion cycle worsens

antecedent: At night, recalling the competition and self-negating thoughts
Daytime low mood and insufficient energy
target_behavior.core_reason: Persistent rumination and anxiety after failure interfere with sleep and daily self-management
target_behavior.function: Short-term avoidance of facing failure and the need for emotional processing
target_behavior.consequence: Physical fitness and energy decline, further weakening training and work performance, forming a vicious cycle
